evidence.title: 日下舊聞考 东宫门
evidence.excerpt_zh: 由鑑園北山徑折而東為東宫門樓宇上下各七楹東向南北朝房各三楹其外為䕶河有石橋（長春園册）臣等謹案東宫門亦稱大東門
evidence.summary: The eastern gate: seven bays on two floors facing east, with three-bay court rooms north and south, a moat and stone bridge beyond. Also called 大東門.

evidence.title: 东宫门, also 大东门, 长春园
evidence.excerpt_zh: 由鑑園北山徑折而東為東宫門樓宇上下各七楹東向南北朝房各三楹其外為䕶河有石橋……東宫門亦稱大東門
evidence.summary: Seven-bay two-storey gate facing east, three-bay offices north and south, moat with a stone bridge outside.

evidence.title: 出大东门启跸成什
evidence.locator: v3 p.237, under 长春园; source ref 6-096
evidence.excerpt_zh: 春露浓瀼始履原，上陵启跸自东门。林端骀荡惠风畅，岭外曈昽晓旭暄。良驈安闲策长陌，耕牛散牧傍前村。由旬路近已前驻，觐吏披章成宪存。
evidence.summary: Poem 出大东门启跸成什 by the Jiaqing Emperor, 1815, filed by the editors under 长春园.

evidence.title: 出大东门启跸作
evidence.locator: v3 p.239, under 长春园; source ref 6-310
evidence.excerpt_zh: 履原春露每萦心，又届上陵节序临。日月推迁岁华速，旰宵思慕考恩深。曈昽红旭升遥墅，灿烂丹霞绘远浔。马度石桥遵大路，翠屏西北列嵚崟。
evidence.summary: Poem 出大东门启跸作 by the Jiaqing Emperor, 1817, filed by the editors under 长春园.

evidence.title: 出大东门启跸成什
evidence.locator: v3 p.240, under 长春园; source ref 7-283
evidence.excerpt_zh: 晓乘良骑启东门，路转清河村北垣。溶漾新波浮远渚，依稀芳草绣平原。闲云不系春山影，余润犹培宿麦根。垅首青青虞践踏，属车申戒保黎元。
evidence.summary: Poem 出大东门启跸成什 by the Jiaqing Emperor, 1820, filed by the editors under 长春园.

evidence.title: 长春园: East Gate, 1860 and after
evidence.excerpt_other: been the one through which Emperor Hsien Feng fled to Jehol in 1860, and to have been rebuilt by the Empress Dowager Tz'u Hsi.
evidence.summary: Said of the east gate of 长春园; oral (Ts'un Feng, Huang Ju Lan). Plate: stone lion guarding the east gate.

evidence.title: Malone on the east gate of 长春园
evidence.summary: Said to be the gate by which Xianfeng left for Jehol in 1860, and to have been rebuilt by Cixi; stone lions, and the bridge. He reports this as hearsay, and so do we.

evidence.title: 《圆明园长春园宫门区遗址发掘报告》
evidence.summary: Report on the Changchun Yuan gate quarter and Danhuai Tang, finding the layout matches the original plan of the garden.

searched: No picture of it found in the Forty Scenes album, its 1745 woodcuts, the Bertin gouaches and the 1887 lithograph; the 20 Xiyang Lou plates; ruin photographs on Commons, at Östasiatiska museet, the Slovene Ethnographic Museum, Historical Photographs of China, the Rijksmuseum, Wellcome and in NDL's albums of about 1900; today's photographs on Commons.
